answer:
**Review of 2 architectures (data-platform team).** The search budget ran out after my second round of searches, so some checks are unverified and I did not run the quota lookup. Where a point rests on weak retrieval, I say so.

## Lakehouse on Apache Iceberg (lakehouse-iceberg, eu-central-1)

Finding 1 [high · Reliability · REL09-BP01] The 140 S3 Tables have no backup (backup: none), the raw layer has no retention, and the RPO is 1440 minutes. The best practice asks for backups, or a way to reproduce the data from sources, that meet the RPO and RTO [S31].

Finding 2 [medium · Operational Excellence · OPS10-BP02] Glue failure alerts are off and max_retries is 0, so a failed nightly job has no defined alert or response path. The guidance is to have a process for each alert [S3].

Finding 3 [medium · Security · SEC08-BP02] Athena query results are not encrypted, and the tables use SSE-S3. The best practice is to enforce encryption at rest [S8]. Key management (KMS key policies, CloudTrail logging of key use) is also worth reviewing [S10].

Finding 4 [medium · Sustainability · MLSUS03-BP01] All 30 Glue jobs run at 02:00 UTC on a fixed schedule. The retrieved guidance names fixed-schedule batch processing as an anti-pattern compared with event-driven pipelines [S28]. Note that this is ML Lens guidance applied by analogy.

No gap found in what I retrieved:
- Lake Formation: IAM allowed principals are off on new tables, and LF-tags are used. This fits least-privilege access [S6].
- Iceberg maintenance: compaction is enabled and snapshots expire after 7 days. Athena's OPTIMIZE and VACUUM cover this [S36].

Not verified: the Athena per-query bytes-scanned cutoff is not set, and the retrieved text did not address it. The Glue concurrency limit (30 jobs at 20 DPUs each) was not checked against a quota.

## Clickstream ingestion (streaming-ingest, eu-central-1)

Finding 5 [high · Reliability · REL10-BP01] OpenSearch runs in one Availability Zone, and the NFR is 99.9% availability. The guidance is to deploy and replicate across multiple AZs [S11].

Finding 6 [medium · Reliability · REL05-BP04] The dead-letter queue has no age alarm and manual redrive. The guidance is to alarm on DLQ volume and message age [S15].

Finding 7 [medium · Reliability · REL09-BP01] Aurora has 1-day backup retention against a 15-minute RPO, and the record does not show point-in-time recovery. Backups must meet the RPO [S31]. Aurora replicates across AZs by default [S11], but it has one writer and no reader replicas.

Finding 8 [medium · Operational Excellence · OPS07-BP03] DLQ redrive is manual, and no runbook is recorded for it. The guidance is to keep runbooks with error handling and escalation steps [S4].

Finding 9 [low · Cost Optimization · COST06-BP01] The record has a $5,000 monthly budget but no cost model. The guidance is to model costs of the workload and its components [S22].

No gap found in what I retrieved:
- Security: Kinesis and Aurora are encrypted with KMS [S10]. OpenSearch encryption and access settings are not in the record, so I did not assess them.

Not verified: the expected peak of 6 MB/s on 4 provisioned shards could not be checked against the per-shard limit, because the quota lookup was not run and the search budget ran out. Lambda has no reserved concurrency, and the retrieved text ties concurrency to shard count and parallelization factor [S18].

Pillars covered: 6 of 6 (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability). Performance Efficiency rests on weak retrieval and the two unverified checks above.

I have not recorded any finding. Tell me which numbers to record (for example "record finding 5") and I will do so.
